answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to lock a small non-transferable stake before transacting, slashed when an identity is caught echoing duplicate bids or fake reviews across accounts. Like a ferrous core that only attracts genuine filings, reputation accrues slowly through verified work, while new identities start on basalt — solid but low-trust ground — and must earn throughput over time. Spinning up thousands of fake agents then costs more than any gain from gaming the market.
